announcements.text: General Motors Defense LLC, Warren, Michigan, was awarded a firm-fixed-price contract for infantry squad vehicles and winch kits. The amount of this action is $142,985,392 with a total cumulative face value of $623,769,043. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of June 24, 2027. Army Contracting Command, Detroit Arsenal, Michigan, is the contracting activity (W912CH-26-F-0339).

CORRECTION: The $17,868,250 firm-fixed-price contract (W912HY-26-C-A020) announced on June 2, 2026, to Mike Hooks LLC, Westlake, Louisiana, for pipeline dredging of the Corpus Christi Ship Channel, was actually awarded on June 5, 2026.

Lockheed Martin, Littleton, Colorado, has been awarded a $514,412,528 modification (P00200) to a previously awarded contract (FA8807-18-C-0009) for the production of Space Vehicles 23 and 24. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $4,683,126,124 from $4,168,713,596. Work will be performed at Littleton, Colorado, and is expected to be completed by Nov. 30, 2032. Fiscal 2026 procurement funds in the amount of $514,412,528 are being obligated at time of award. The Space Systems Command’s Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Contracting Division, Los Angeles, California, is the contracting activity.

Benaka Inc., New Brunswick, New Jersey (FA2835-26-D-0003); Campbell Construction Group LLC, Peabody, Massachusetts (FA2835-26-D-0006); Doyon Technical Services LLC, Federal Way, Washington (FA2835-26-D-0004); McKenzie Construction & Site Development LLC, Washington, D.C. (FA2835-26-D-0007); and Veterans Development Corp. Inc., Norwell, Massachusetts (FA2835-26-D-0005), were awarded a ceiling $71,875,939 multiple award, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for construction. This contract provides for a contract vehicle to complete complex construction requirements that involve multiple trades and skill mixes. Work will be performed at Hanscom Air Force Base, Bedford, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by June 10, 2031. These contracts were competitive acquisitions and 18 offers were received. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance funds in the amount of $1,475,137 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Operational Contracting Division, Hanscom AFB, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity.

Blane International Group, Cumming, Georgia (FA2823-26-D-0009); Iron Horse Logistics, Durango, Colorado (FA2823-26-D-0010); Light As Air Boats LLC, Largo, Florida (FA2823-26-D-0011); Quantico Tactical Inc., Aberdeen, North Carolina (FA2823-26-D-0012); and Victory Procurement Services LLC, Huntsville, Alabama (FA2823-26-D-0013), were awarded a ceiling $49,999,999 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the acquisition of watercraft targets. This contract provides for the acquisition of watercraft targets. Work will be performed at Cumming, Georgia; Durango, Colorado; Largo, Florida; Aberdeen, North Carolina; and Huntsville, Alabama, and is expected to be completed by June 14, 2031. These contracts were competitive acquisitions and six offers were received. Fiscal 2025 and 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $750 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Test Center, Eglin Air Force Base, Florida, is the contracting activity.

General Atomics-Integrated Intelligence Inc., Charlottesville, Virginia, has been awarded a ceiling $49,723,164 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for GALAWAR. This contract provides for the development of electromagnetic spectrum sensing and geolocation capabilities in support of battlespace situational awareness. Work will be performed at Charlottesville, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by Aug. 11, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition and one offer was received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $25,000 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, New York, is the contracting activity (FA8750-26-C-B016).

Rohde & Schwarz USA Inc., Columbia, Maryland, has been awarded a $20,211,163 firm-fixed-price requirements contract for the purchase of versatile diagnostic automatic test station kits. This contract provides for kits required to assemble standardized, commercially available test equipment, components, and software. Work will be performed at Robins Air Force Base, Georgia, and is expected to be completed by June 11, 2031. This contract was a sole source acquisition. No funds are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Sustainment Center, Robins AFB, Georgia, is the contracting activity (FA8579-26-D-0002).

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Linthicum Heights, Maryland, has been awarded a $14,215,800 modification (P00178) to previously awarded FA8615-17-C-6047 for Active Electronically Scanned Array radars of Air Force F-16 aircraft. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $1,836,144,779 from $1,821,928,979. Work will be performed at Linthicum Heights, Maryland, and is expected to be completed by May 31, 2031. Fiscal 2024 procurement funds in the amount of $2,843,160; fiscal 2026 procurement funds in the amount of $8,529,480; and fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $2,843,160, are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity.

(N6852026D1037); StrongAI Solutions*, Henderson, Nevada (N6852026D1038); International Business Machines Corp., Bethesda, Maryland (N6852026D1039); Ascentium LLC,* Fairfax, Virginia (N6852026D1040); High Side Technology,* Johns Island, South Carolina (N6852026D1041); Lockheed Martin Corp., Orlando, Florida (N6852026D1042); TrustedQA Inc.,* Reston, Virginia (N6852026D1043); G2IT LLC,* Annapolis, Maryland (N6852026D1044); Desi-Spalding JV,* Lexington Park, Maryland (N6852026D1045); Spalding Consulting Inc., Lexington Park, Maryland (N6852026D10456); Accelint Global Inc., San Diego, California (N6852026D10457); Naval Systems Inc., Lexington Park, Maryland (N6852026D1048); Accelint Intelligent Systems LLC, Mullica Hill, New Jersey (N6852026D1049); Accenture Federal Services LLC, Arlington, Virginia (N6852026D1050); Cornerstone Bestica Federal Service LLC,* Honolulu, Hawaii (N6852026D1051); Technik Inc.,* Herndon, Virginia (N6852026D1052); Allies LLC,* Lexington Park, Maryland (N6852026D1053); CTM JV LLC, Hollywood, Maryland (N6852026D1054); Plateau Software Inc.,* Fairfax, Virginia (N6852026D1055); The Kenific Group LLC,* Leesburg, Virginia (N6852026D1056); DLH LLC, Bethesda, Maryland (N6852026D1057); Atechgov LLC,* Bethesda, Maryland (N6852026D1058); Basecamp Consulting and Solutions LLC,* Reston, Virginia (N6852026D1059); 22nd Century Technologies Inc., McLean, Virginia (N6852026D1060); Response AI Solutions,* Arlington, Virginia (N6852026D1061); and Intercon LLC,* Fredericksburg, Virginia (N6852026D1062), are awarded firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost reimbursable, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contracts with an estimated aggregate ceiling of $249,900,000. These contracts provide for capability modernization, deployment, and support for Naval maintenance, repair, and overhaul; Naval supply chain management; Naval product lifecycle management; logistics integrated data environment; and integration and infrastructure capability solutions within the Integrated Platform and Development, Security, and Operations pipeline. The effort will modernize and sustain enterprise information technology systems that support Navy maintenance and logistics operations, improve data integration and accessibility across the naval enterprise, and accelerate the development and deployment of software capabilities to the fleet. Work will be performed at the contractor's location which will be determined as individual orders are issued and is expected to be completed in June 2031. No funds will be obligated at the time of award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. The contracts were competed in two lots (Lot A - open competition and Lot B - small business set aside), 72 offers were received. Commander, Fleet Readiness Center, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Bechtel Plant Machinery Inc., Monroeville, Pennsylvania, was awarded a $128,400,000 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification to a previously awarded contract (N00024-24-C-2114) for Naval Nuclear Propulsion components. Work will be performed in Monroeville, Pennsylvania (36%); and Schenectady, New York (64%), and is expected to be completed by September 2035. Non-appropriated funds in the amount of $128,400,000 were obligated at time of award and funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Castelion Corp.,* Torrance, California, is awarded a $23,350,000 firm-fixed-price order (N6833526F1138) against a previously issued basic ordering agreement (N6833526G0006). This order is for the production and delivery of fifty early operational capability pre-production prototypes and fifty storage and shipping containers to the Navy in support of Small Business Innovation Research Phase III effort, topic AF231-D026, entitled “Low Cost Highly Manufacturable Long Range Strike Weapon Production”, in support of advancing the key enabling technology for a rapidly fieldable hypersonic weapon system. Work will be performed in Rio Rancho, New Mexico (75%); and Torrance, California (25%), and is expected to be completed in December 2027. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $23,350,000 will be obligated at the time of award, none of which will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract action was competed. Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division, Lakehurst, New Jersey, is the contracting activity.

Walashek Industrial & Marine Inc.,* Norfolk, Virginia, is awarded a $9,723,782 firm-fixed-price level-of-effort modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-26-C-4434) to exercise an option for the accomplishment of maintenance, modernization and repair of the steam propulsion plant systems on USS Iwo Jima (LHD 7) during the scheduled fiscal 2026 selected restricted availability. Work will be performed in Norfolk, Virgina, and is expected to be completed by May 2028. Fiscal 2026 other procurement, (Navy) funds in the amount of $9,723,782 will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

US Foods Inc., doing business as US Foods - Los Angeles, La Mirada, California, has been awarded a maximum $166,967,289 firm-fixed-price with economic-price-adjustment, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for full-line food and beverage items. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a 329-day bridge contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is May 8, 2027. Using military service is Navy. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE300-26-D-3020).

M M Manufacturing LLC,** Lajas, Puerto Rico, has been awarded a maximum $13,242,668 modification (P00016) exercising the third one‐year option period of a one‐year base contract (SPE1C1‐23‐D‐0070) with four one‐year option periods for various types of coats and trousers. This is a firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract. The ordering period end date is June 23, 2027. Using military services are Army and Air Force. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2027 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
